clue.text: Dent-ist or painter?

definitions.meaning: one who makes dents, read as a maker of marks pressed into a surface
an artist of the Monet school, catching light and fleeting effects

explanation.definitionFit: A dent is a mark pressed in, so its maker is jokily an 'ist' of such marks, and Monet's school of painters bears the same name.

clue.text: Explorer's company coming in to spoil game

indicators.note: the company arrives in the middle, so its letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: to spoil is to mar
polo is a game played on horseback

explanation.surface: A firm muscles in and ruins a match for a famous traveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The Venetian traveller who reached Kublai Khan's court is the archetypal explorer.

clue.text: Take repaired tyre and have another go

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for 'take', on prescriptions

indicators.note: repaired means put back together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist gets the mended tyre and tries again.
explanation.definitionFit: To try again is simply to have another attempt.

clue.text: Ship carrying a champion Mastersinger

indicators.note: the ship holds the other letters inside it, as cargo

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
CH is the abbreviation for champion, as in dog shows

explanation.surface: A vessel has a prizewinning singer on board.
explanation.walkthrough: Hans Sachs is the cobbler-poet hero of Wagner's opera The Mastersingers of Nuremberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Hans Sachs was a real sixteenth-century master singer of Nuremberg, a member of the guild of poet-musicians.

clue.text: Complex, in an instant, almost consumed

indicators.note: almost means the word falls one letter short, losing its last

parts.note: in a trice means in an instant, so a trice is an instant
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Something complicated got eaten up in a flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Intricate and complex are synonyms for something with many tangled parts.

clue.text: Startled men ran to end of lane — no great distance!

indicators.note: startled men are thrown into disorder, so the letters are scrambled
end of picks the final letter of the word lane

explanation.surface: Frightened men sprint to the end of the lane, though it is hardly far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Startled' rearranges MENRANTO into NANOMETR; 'end of lane' adds E.
explanation.definitionFit: A billionth of a metre is a tiny length, the very opposite of a long way.

clue.text: Extremely pleasant? Not entirely, judging by the sound

indicators.note: not entirely means the phrase is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: extremely pleasant is so nice

explanation.surface: Someone hears something and judges it only partly agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' takes the last E off SO NICE. 'Extremely' looks like a first-and-last selection but is part of the phrase 'so nice'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sonic means relating to sound, so it describes what is judged by ear.

clue.text: Scrooge fit to occupy minor novel

indicators.note: to occupy means to sit inside, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: minor means lesser, less
Scrooge is the Dickens miser, so a byword for one
fit means able

explanation.surface: A Dickensian skinflint is fit to fill a minor role in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo's long work about Jean Valjean is a famous French book of fiction.

clue.text: Favouring a share of activity, or a great increase in activity?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
life, as in a place full of life, means activity
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Someone backs a fair share of the work, or else a great burst of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Phi uses 'activity' twice on purpose: once in the wordplay, where 'of' turns the phrase round so the activity comes before its share, and once in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Proliferation is rapid multiplication or spreading, a sharp rise in the amount of something going on.

clue.text: Unreliable fellow about to desert?

indicators.note: about means round, so the man's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Eric stands for any fellow, a man's name
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: A man who may abandon his post can't be relied on.
explanation.definitionFit: Erratic means irregular and unpredictable, so not to be relied upon.

clue.text: Woodworker's decisive victory, right?

parts.note: a ten-one win is a crushing scoreline

explanation.surface: A carpenter boasts of a crushing win, asking for agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenoner is a craftsman or machine that cuts the projecting tongues of mortise joints in carpentry.

clue.text: Glum, low, definitely disheartened

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: disheartened means the word loses its heart, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone feels down, really dejected.
explanation.definitionFit: Glum and moody both describe a sulky, low-spirited temper.

clue.text: South-east's claim is disputed, regarding earthquake

parts.note: SE is the abbreviation for south-east

indicators.note: a disputed claim is argued over, so its letters are thrown around

explanation.surface: A region's territorial claim is contested, in a matter of tremors.
explanation.definitionFit: Seismical is an older form of seismic, pertaining to earth tremors.

clue.text: Emotionless type mostly to remain without love

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the shortened word goes round the other letter
mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: to stick is to stay or remain
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An unfeeling person mostly stays put, lacking affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, not lacking: STIC (STICK less its last letter) is wrapped round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stoic in the philosophical sense endures pain without showing feeling.

clue.text: Governor putting girl in prison

indicators.note: the girl is put in the prison, so her name goes inside

parts.note: the can is slang for prison
Stella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A ruler has a young woman locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: A castellan is the keeper or commander of a castle, its appointed head.

clue.text: Best for a hint of English cooking?

definitions.text: Best for a hint of English cooking?

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are worked up together and rearranged
a hint of a word is just its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone asks what would best suggest English cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges BESTFORA with E, the 'hint of English'; the whole clue also defines the dish.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sunday joint of beef cooked in the oven is the classic national dish, so it gives the best taste of English food.

clue.text: A red nose's mistakenly showing driving skill

indicators.note: mistakenly means the letters are set out wrongly, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A drink-flushed nose wrongly suggests competence behind the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Road sense is a driver's instinctive awareness of traffic and hazards.

clue.text: Oarsmen perhaps go it and seem prostrated round end of reach

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go around the next one
prostrated means laid low and knocked over, so the letters are tumbled
end of takes the last letter of the word reach

explanation.surface: Rowers push themselves and seem to collapse at the end of a stretch of river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prostrated' turns GOITSEEM into EIGTSOME, which goes 'round' H, the 'end of reach'. A reach is a stretch of river.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome is a group of eight, as a rowing eight crew is.

clue.text: The top view of the city?

definitions.text: The top view of the city?

parts.words: The top view of the city?
parts.note: reads like a viewpoint from high above, but means a city panorama made of the upper surfaces of buildings

explanation.definitionFit: The skyline of tiles, chimneys and slates seen from above forms a vista of house tops.

clue.text: Composer's anger about line being repressed

indicators.note: the line is held down inside the angry word, so it goes within
about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: anger means rage

explanation.surface: A musician's fury is about a line being held down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns RAGE into EGAR, and 'being repressed' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edward Elgar wrote the Enigma Variations, an English composer.

clue.text: Strike's foundation mostly seen in part of London

parts.note: to batter is to strike repeatedly

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: a seat is a base or foundation

explanation.surface: A strike's mostly hidden roots are found in a London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'has': BATTER has SEA, i.e. SEAT shortened by 'mostly'. Battersea is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district on the south bank of the Thames, known for its power station.

clue.text: Stupid person brought in to a poet…

indicators.note: brought in means placed within the other word

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A fool is introduced to a versifier.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso wrote Jerusalem Delivered, an Italian Renaissance epic poem.

clue.text: 2…a stupid person upset and stand-offish

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a fool is a stupid person

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a fool is upset and keeps away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns FOOL into LOOF. The ellipsis carries on the previous clue's surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant and cool in manner, keeping others at arm's length.

clue.text: Some Schubert etc obviously recalled here

definitions.text: Some Schubert etc obviously recalled here

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the run is read backwards
some means only part of these words is used, a hidden run

explanation.surface: A listener notes that some Schubert is clearly remembered here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes TETCO from 'schuberT ETC Obviously', and 'recalled' turns it round. Schubert wrote a famous Octet.
explanation.definitionFit: Schubert's Octet in F is a well-known piece for eight players.

clue.text: Antelope overturning one pen

indicators.note: overturning in a down clue turns the whole run upside down, so backwards

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral
a Biro is a ballpoint pen, a British trade name

explanation.surface: A grazer knocks over a single pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African grazing antelope of the savanna.

clue.text: Revolutionary line is taken in no letter

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned right round, so the whole is read backwards
taken in means held inside the word for no

parts.note: nope is a casual no

explanation.surface: A radical political line is rejected in a written note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts LIS inside NOPE to give NOLISPE, which 'Revolutionary' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsilon is the fifth character of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: River with gold fish, tailless, going round in ring

annotationWithheld.why: River with gold fish, tailless, going round in ring: OR (gold) + IN + O + CO(D) accounts for the letters, but no reading gives both 'going round' and 'ring' a job without an extra O
annotationWithheld.clue: River with gold fish, tailless, going round in ring

clue.text: Serving area in better condition, we hear? One's given a false view

parts.note: a counter is where customers are served in a shop

indicators.note: we hear means the next part is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: fitter means in better shape

explanation.surface: A shop counter in better shape gives a misleading impression.
explanation.definitionFit: A forger passes off fakes, presenting a false picture of what is genuine.
